newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU seen agreeing modified cotton dumping plan.
newsitem.headline: EU seen agreeing modified cotton dumping plan.

text.p: The European Union is likely to agree later on Friday a modified plan for definitive anti-dumping duties on cotton imports from China, Egypt, India, Indonesia, Turkey and Pakistan, EU officials and diplomats said.

One EU official said national capitals had until 1600 (1400 GMT) to accept or reject the European Commission's modified proposal for duties on unbleached cotton fabric imports from the countries named.

The EU ambassadors seemed set to reject the plan after a first meeting on Thursday but after a second meeting later in the day a Commission spokesman said there was "quite a strong likelihood" of agreement.
Diplomats said after the first meeting that nine of the EU's 15 states had rejected the proposal, making it likely the plan would lapse come the May 20 expiry date for provisional duties.
But a Commission offer to review the duties after one year appeared to have swung at least two countries behind the six who originally backed the plan.
Belgium, Greece, Spain, France, Italy and Portugal supported the proposal earlier on Thursday, two countries shy of the simple majority needed to impose final duties.

"The Commission saw how finely balanced the thing was," the spokesman said in reference both to EU countries' positions and to the conflicting positions on duties of EU cotton producers and cotton finishers.
"The best thing for the Commission to do was to modify the proposal so that a full review can take place within the shortest possible time -- That is to say one year," he added.

Duties remained unchanged from provisional ones, he said, meaning the Chinese-origin imports face 18.9 percent duties, those from Egypt 13 percent, India 17.2 percent, Indonesia 14.5 percent, Pakistan 22.9 percent and Turkey 17.5 percent.
Companies which have cooperated with EU dumping officials' inquiries generally face reduced rates.
One EU diplomat expressed amazement at the turnaround.
"We can only guess that pressures on the Commission have been excessive," the diplomat said.
The Commission imposed provisional duties against grey cotton fabrics from the six named countries last November, setting in train the further review period expiring on May 20.
